data.hypothesis: The unannotated-builtin and target-local candidates were both valid, had the same reported binary SHA-256, and measured 8.1694e-05 s and 8.1894e-05 s respectively. This candidate applies target("popcnt") only to the helper, leaving run generic. If GCC does not inline across the target-feature boundary, the recurrence may incur a helper call; if it does inline, generated code may remain indistinguishable. The official measurement will test this annotation-scope assumption without claiming a speedup.

memory_lessons.applicability: Use the measured builtin and target-local candidates as comparators; their identical binary hashes do not establish a performance difference between implementations.
memory_lessons.claim: The unannotated-builtin candidate and target-local candidate were both correct and measured close in time (8.1694e-05 s versus 8.1894e-05 s), with the same binary SHA-256. The measurements do not show a meaningful advantage for either version.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure whether limiting target("popcnt") to the helper changes the generic caller's generated code or runtime.
